title: Build on Arrival
story:
```
[nightly] 03:00:01 docker build -t ingest-dev ./ingest      OK
[nightly] 03:00:09 docker run -d -p 8110:8000 kestrel/ingest:dev
[nightly] 03:00:09 Unable to find image 'kestrel/ingest:dev' locally
[nightly] 03:00:10 docker: pull access denied for kestrel/ingest
[nightly] 03:00:10 FATAL: ingest bay is dark
```

Ingrid pinned this above the coffee machine. Amara's nightly script builds one tag and runs another, so the ingest bay for the radiometer data has been dark for three nights. She wants build and run to stop disagreeing: a Compose project `ingest-bay` with one service `ingest`, built from the `./ingest` folder and tagged `kestrel/ingest:dev`.
objectives: Service `ingest` builds from `./ingest` and is tagged `kestrel/ingest:dev`
It publishes host port 8110 to container port 8000
Run it so image `kestrel/ingest:dev` exists and http://localhost:8110 answers
startingState: `/workspace/ingest/` holds a working Dockerfile and `app.py`; no image has been built.
hints: A Compose service can carry a `build:` instruction instead of only pulling an image, so Compose builds it for you during `up`. If the service also has an `image:` key, that key becomes the name the built image receives.
Under the service use `build: ./ingest` (the folder containing the Dockerfile) together with `image: kestrel/ingest:dev`. Then `docker compose up -d --build` builds and starts it in one go.

Save this as `compose.yaml` and run `docker compose up -d --build`:

```yaml
name: ingest-bay
services:
  ingest:
    build: ./ingest
    image: kestrel/ingest:dev
    ports:
      - "8110:8000"
```

files.content:
FROM python:3.12-alpine
WORKDIR /srv
COPY app.py .
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["python", "app.py"]

from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer


class Bay(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        self.send_response(200)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b"INGEST READY: radiometer feed open\n")


HTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", 8000), Bay).serve_forever()

validation.description: http://localhost:8110 reports the ingest bay is ready

solution:
cat > compose.yaml <<'EOF'
name: ingest-bay
services:
  ingest:
    build: ./ingest
    image: kestrel/ingest:dev
    ports:
      - "8110:8000"
EOF
debrief: With `build:` plus `image:`, Compose is the single source of truth for both how an image is made and what it is called, so scripts can no longer drift apart. Pro tip: `docker compose build` only builds, and `docker compose up -d --build` forces a rebuild after you edit code -- plain `up` reuses an existing image.
